thread:
sara: Heads-up — EU1 queue depth just spiked for rdm-13b-quant on the p4d pool. 2.4x baseline, p95 ~90s. tagging eng-infra and oncall.

matt: Ack. seeing same in dashboards. Which models are hot?

sara: rdm-13b-quant is the primary offender, then rdm-7b-fp16 shows a small bump.

kai: Past 10m hist (quick):
```
model,rq_depth,p95_latency
rdm-13b-quant,240,92s
rdm-7b-fp16,60,28s
embed-2,12,120ms
```
Looks like continuous backlog, not just a burst.

lina: Any unusual traffic origin? customer/route?

sara: Mostly /v1/generate from a handful of high-throughput API keys (team: growth and search experiments). Not a prod customer flood.

matt: Oncall runbook step 1: confirm capacity signals and admission control. Kai, can you check the admission-controller logs and active leases?

kai: Checking now. quick outputs:
```
# kubectl -n inference-eu1 get pods
NAME                           READY   STATUS
admission-controller-0         1/1     Running
serve-pool-p4d-0               16/16   Running
serve-pool-p4d-1               16/16   Running
```
No respawn churn. Admission controller shows backpressure kicks but backlog keeps growing.

oncall-bot: paging eng-infra oncall (rotation: matt). Incident severity: S2 - queue buildup.

matt: Thanks. Next: try a temporary policy tweak to allow smaller batch sizes for rdm-13b-quant or divert lower-priority keys to the cheaper rdm-7b-fp16. Sara, can you list the top 5 API keys by qps?

sara: Top keys: growth-experiments, search-sim, demo-automations, partner-sandbox, internal-tools (ordered). growth-experiments ~38% of incoming QPS.

lina: Proposal: enforce per-key soft rate limits for growth-experiments + move that key to the lower-cost model for the next 12m while we mitigate. That keeps latency SLOs for other customers.

matt: I can push a temporary route policy: priority=low for growth-experiments and fallback model=rdm-7b-fp16. Will do 2-min canary then 100% if stable.

kai: Also suggest flipping admission-controller to stricter admission for long requests (>512 tokens). Add a temporary token ceiling of 512 for rdm-13b-quant to preserve throughput.

sara: Agree. Also, can we enable prefix/KV cache for search-sim? I see repeated prompts. That would save tokens quickly.

matt: On it. Will execute the plan: 1) enable per-key soft throttle for growth-experiments -> fallback to 7b, 2) set max_tokens=512 for rdm-13b-quant admissions, 3) enable prefix caching for search-sim.

devops-bot: running policy change: apply /policies/temporary/eu1-backpressure-1778001123.json

devops-bot: policy rollout: canary 10% -> ok after 120s -> 100% applied

matt: Canary looks fine, p95 for other keys holding. Increasing canary to 100%.

kai: Admission-controller tweak applied. Observed immediate drop in queue depth for rdm-13b-quant from 240 -> 98 in ~3m. p95 down to 34s.

sara: Nice. Cost note: if we keep fallback to 7b for growth-experiments for an hour, estimates show ~18% cost reduction for that traffic.

lina: Good tradeoff. We should open a follow-up doc to discuss dedicated capacity or reserved burst for growth tests — this pattern repeats.

matt: Agreed. Action items:
- matt: keep policy for 60m, monitor p95 and queue depth (done).
- kai: collect admission-controller logs + export for postmortem (ETA 1h).
- sara: reach out to growth team to throttle experiments and schedule a short runbook sync.
- lina: create ticket for capacity planning (dedicated burst vs routing rules).

sara: I'll ping growth now.

matt: If backlog reappears after policy rollback, we'll escalate to provisioning additional dedicated capacity (requires sales approval for reserve commit).

oncall-bot: incident update queued: severity S2 -> monitoring, actions applied.

lina: We should track this under "capacity-signals" for trend analysis. Add tags: eu1, rdm-13b, backpressure, policy-fallback.

sara: Will add tags + attach the earliest metric graphs.

kai: For the postmortem, I'll include a small script to correlate per-key QPS vs admission rates so product can limit experimental QPS in future.

matt: Thanks team. re-eval in 45m unless things regress. :thumbsup:

sara: closing thread for now, will reopen if queue grows. :white_check_mark:
